overlap.note: the categories overlap: the candidates accepted by the checks include those outside the pool limit, and a candidate can be both excluded by requirements and failed numerically; the counts need not sum to the pool size

agent.label: QuinticDamping
agent.reason: Recommend QuinticDamping: its training-only fit gave validation RMSE 0.0712333 Y and four-fold trajectory-grouped diagnostic RMSE 0.0543695 Y, compared with 0.0728230 Y / 0.0557991 Y for TrigDamping and 0.0759100 Y / 0.0557450 Y for StaticBlend. Y is the unknown output unit. These small differences are not statistically decisive; it is recommended for its consistent held-trajectory output accuracy, not a proven physical spring interpretation. All three delivered candidates were subsequently refitted on both supplied files, so their final validation-file errors are in-sample. Grouped diagnostics use the final coefficients as numerical warm starts and reuse structure/smoothing choices screened on these files; they are not a completely untouched assessment. Quintic extrapolation can be stiff and have extra equilibria; the trigonometric model is the simpler bounded-force alternative.

ranking.label: oracle-based selection on test data
ranking.note: This ranking selects on the test data. It measures whether the pool contains an accurate model, not whether the agent can recognize that model without test data. A rank is not evidence of physical admissibility: each entry carries its unresolved requirements and any violation allowed by the user.
ranking.tie_rule: |S_a - S_b| <= 1e-12 * max(S_a, S_b) for consecutive candidates; tied candidates share a rank

settings.discontinuities: expressions with jumps (Piecewise, sign) are evaluated pointwise at the sample instants and Runge-Kutta stages; no event detection or step refinement is applied at a jump
